chapter: Kansas City, Basie, Prez and Booker Pittman
title: Sleeping in Paseo Park and Street's Poolhall
summary: Stranded again, the musicians sleep in the park and use Street's Poolhall as an address, while Budd hides his plight from his father.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: So we got stranded. We had to finally get out of the apartment at 13th and Lydia, and so we took the park for our beds, and we used Street's Poolhall for our home address, because I didn't want to let my mother know I was stranded. My father had told me, he says, "You leave home 'cause you ain't going to get nowhere here in Dallas, if you want to embark on music." And he says, "If you can't make it I'll send for you." So I didn't want to tell him that I wasn't making it, because I knew he would make me come home.
That's the story of my life, too.
So we used Street's Poolhall as our mailing address, and we slept --
That's right, and we slept in the park, Paseo Park, by night.
That's right back of Street's Pool-
That's right. You are familiar with that, I must say.
Very much so. We paid the same dues. Yeah. (Inaudible.)
